1️⃣ Phở 10 Lý Quốc Sư
📍 10 Lý Quốc Sư, Hoàn Kiếm (~$2.70 - $3.80)
Iconic beef phở with slow-simmered bone broth and tender beef slices right by St. Joseph’s Cathedral.

2️⃣ Tuyết Bún Chả 34

3️⃣ Phở Gà Nguyệt

Legendary chicken phở stall. Don’t miss their dry chicken phở (phở gà trộn) with tender chicken, fried shallots & crushed peanuts!

Only have time for three things in Hanoi? Here’s how to spend it 🇻🇳✨

If you’re visiting Hanoi for the first time or only have 24–48 hours, don’t rush to check off ten different tourist traps. Slow down and focus on these three experiences:

1️⃣ Find a little local food spot 🍜
Start your morning with a steaming bowl of phở bò, or pull up a low plastic stool for smoky bún chả at lunch. Take your time, watch the street outside, and soak in the little details around you.

2️⃣ Stop for Vietnamese coffee ☕
Whether it’s rich egg coffee (cà phê trứng) or a slow-dripped cà phê sữa đá, find a cozy corner where you can watch Hanoi life drift by. Sometimes the best part of exploring is taking a break.

3️⃣ Discover the city on foot 🏮
Take an easy walk around Hoàn Kiếm Lake, then let yourself wander into the maze of the Old Quarter. Look up at the French colonial balconies, peek down the narrow alleys, and always take the scenic route.

Ordering your first coffee in Hanoi can feel like a guessing game. ☕

Here is a quick guide so you get exactly what you want:

1. Hot or iced: Say “nóng” for hot, or “đá” for iced.
2. Milk choice: In Vietnam, milk coffee (“cà phê sữa”) means sweet condensed milk by default. If you prefer fresh milk, ask for “sữa tươi”.
3. Sweetness: Vietnamese coffee is naturally bold and sweet. Ask for “ít ngọt” (less sweet) before the barista starts brewing.
4. Not sure? Just point to the menu and ask what is inside. People are happy to help.

Pro move: Vietnamese coffee uses Robusta beans, which carry about twice the caffeine of Arabica. Take your time with those first few sips.

Ordering your first coffee in Hanoi can feel like a guessing game. ☕

Here is a quick guide so you get exactly what you want:

1. Hot or iced: Say “nóng” for hot, or “đá” for iced.
2. Milk choice: In Vietnam, milk coffee (“cà phê sữa”) means sweet condensed milk by default. If you prefer fresh milk, ask for “sữa tươi”.
3. Sweetness: Vietnamese coffee is naturally bold and sweet. Ask for “ít ngọt” (less sweet) before the barista starts brewing.
4. Not sure? Just point to the menu and ask what is inside. People are happy to help.

Pro move: Vietnamese coffee uses Robusta beans, which carry about twice the caffeine of Arabica. Take your time with those first few sips.

data.description: The number of unique accounts that have seen your content, at least once, including in ads. Content includes posts, stories, reels, videos and live videos. Reach is different from impressions, which may include multiple views of your content by the same accounts. This metric is estimated and in development.

data.name: views
data.title: Views
data.description: The number of times your content was played or displayed. Content includes reels, posts, stories.

data.name: profile_views
data.title: Profile visits
data.description: The number of times that your profile was visited.

data.name: website_clicks
data.title: Website link taps
data.description: The number of times that the link to your website was tapped.

data.name: total_interactions
data.title: Content interactions
data.description: The total number of post interactions, story interactions, reels interactions, video interactions and live video interactions, including any interactions on boosted content.

data.name: accounts_engaged
data.title: Accounts engaged
data.description: The number of accounts that have interacted with your content, including in ads. Content includes posts, stories, reels, videos and live videos. Interactions can include actions such as likes, saves, comments, shares or replies. These metrics are estimated and in development.
